title: Chiefs release first renderings of new stadium in Kansas set to open in 2031
content:
The Kansas City Chiefs released initial renderings Wednesday of their new $3 billion domed stadium in Kansas, which is set to open in 2031. The team also announced Wednesday that it had selected Kansas City-based company MANICA as the lead architect firm for the project.

Chiefs owner Clark Hunt, in a release Wednesday, said many details were still to come regarding the stadium, but said he believed the final result would be “spectacular.”

“From the beginning, our goal has been to build something that improved the gameday experience for every single fan,” Hunt said. “This new stadium will do just that.”

Hunt added that the new Chiefs stadium would hold at least 70,000 fans, and promised it would “still be the best place in the world to tailgate,” while also being built to enhance fan noise.

Initial renderings show a stadium design with many similarities to the current Arrowhead Stadium bowl, which includes three decks of seats. The biggest difference is a translucent roof on top, providing weather control that will enable the Chiefs to aggressively bid on major sporting events, such as Final Fours and the Super Bowl.

The Chiefs first announced their plans to move to Kansas City, Kan., during a gathering at the Kansas State Capitol in December. Lieutenant Gov. David Toland called it “the largest economic win in Kansas history,” adding that “this win will also cement Kansas as a global destination for sports and entertainment.”

The Chiefs’ current lease at Truman Sports Complex — home of Arrowhead Stadium — expires in January 2031. The team is set to play its games at that site through the 2030 season.

Crossing state lines means the Chiefs will be moving on from one of the NFL’s most historic venues. Built in 1972, Arrowhead is the third-oldest stadium in the league, behind only Chicago’s Soldier Field and Green Bay’s Lambeau Field.

The Chiefs have been playing in Kansas City, Mo., since 1963, when then-owner Lamar Hunt moved his Dallas Texans AFL franchise north and renamed the team.
